title.narrative: Multi sectoral response to emergency Protection, Health and GBV needs of conflict-affected populations in Khersonska and Kharkivska

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe proposed complementary multi-sectoral project will meet the basic emergency needs of conflict affected populations in rural zones and areas most affected by the conflict in Kharkivska and Khersonska. The 12-months intervention will reach a total of 57085 direct beneficiaries (25258 women, 3219 girls, 25322men and 3376 boys).ltbrgt The Action, a collaborative effort between INTERSOS and Light of Hope (LoH), is a comprehensive response designed to address the complex challenges faced by vulnerable populations. It initiates community engagement through a participatory approach, leveraging Community Based Protection Officers (CBPOs) and Outreach Facilitators (OFs). Daily information sessions and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) cover critical topics such as Housing, Land, and Property rights, community entitlements, and relevant laws. A dedicated hotline managed by Social Workers facilitates confidential reporting and inquiries, fostering community participation. The client-centered case management approach, including legal counselling and psychosocial support, underscores the commitment to protecting beneficiaries' health, safety, and overall resilience.ltbrgtA focal point of the program is addressing GBV risks and providing tailored solutions. Social workers, adhering to Inter-Agency Standard Operational Procedures on Gender-Based Violence Case Management, offer a survivor-centered response. Psychosocial support services, both individual and group-based, are delivered to GBV survivors and those at risk. Cash and voucher assistance, dignity kits safety audits, assessment of barriers in accessing services and awareness sessions contribute to a holistic GBV prevention and response strategy.ltbrgtThe integrated health approach encompasses various activities aimed at enhancing access to quality and comprehensive health care. Medical Mobile Units (MMUs) provide primary health care, prioritizing vulnerable populations in challenging areas. Health promoters engage in community outreach, focusing on health promotion topics such as the management and prevention of Non-Communicable Disease (NCD), communicable diseases, sexual and reproductive health, and winterization measures. Capacity building for health care providers, first responders, and community members ensures a robust health response. Emergency response capacity and adaptability are emphasized through comprehensive needs assessments, aligning with international standards. ltbrgtIn line with the Allocation’s commitment to meaningful local partnerships and INTERSOS’ Localisation strategy, INTERSOS works in close collaboration with LoH in Kharkiv throughout the project cycle and has adopted an equal cost sharing policy. The aim of this collaboration is to build upon previous capacity strengthening of LoH and move towards sustainable future localised implementation. ltbrgtlt/pgt
